Commission Guide

UCBA 2026 + RUNDBA (New Development) — Simplified reference for agents

Disclaimer: This is a simplified summary for quick reference only. Always refer to the full UCBA and RUNDBA agreements for binding terms. Commissions are not set by law and are fully negotiable. Source: REBNY UCBA January 2026 revision + RUNDBA Exhibit D (copyright 2025).

How Commission Works

1

Commission is negotiable — Not set by law. Agreed between parties before or at the time of engagement.

2

Earned at closing — Commission is earned ONLY when the deal fully closes and money changes hands. No closing = no commission.

3

Paid by different parties — Seller, buyer, landlord, tenant, or split. Depends on deal type and agreement.

4

Split with brokerage — Your commission is your agreed split with Mallan Real Estate. Submit a commission request in the "Track Deal / Commissions" tab.

Deal Types at a Glance

Resale (Existing Building)
Co-broke via RLS
New Development (Sponsor)
RUNDBA agreement
Rental
OP / TP / Split
Buyer-Paid Commission
Buyer broker agreement required

Key Terms

Co-Broke: Commission offered by listing brokerage to buyer's agent via RLS.
UCBA: Universal Co-Brokerage Agreement — REBNY's rules governing how brokerages cooperate.
RUNDBA: Universal New Development Brokerage Agreement — governs new dev sponsor deals.
Exclusive Sales Agent: The brokerage appointed by the sponsor to sell new dev units.
Outside Broker: You (the agent/brokerage bringing a buyer to a new development).
Net Purchase Price: Sale price minus credits, concessions, and incentives. Commission calculated on this.
OP (Owner Pays): Landlord pays the full broker fee on a rental.
TP (Tenant Pays): Tenant pays the broker fee on a rental.
Procuring Cause: The agent who was instrumental in bringing about the sale. Required for commission.

Resale (Existing Building) — Co-Broke Commission

When you bring a buyer to another brokerage's listing via REBNY RLS

How It Works

  1. Listing agent sets co-broke amount when entering listing on RLS
  2. You (buyer's agent) see the listing and the co-broke offered
  3. You show the property to your buyer client
  4. Deal goes under contract and closes
  5. Listing brokerage pays co-broke to your brokerage at closing
  6. You receive your split from the brokerage

What You Need

  • Buyer Broker Agreement (signed before showing)
  • Active NY real estate license
  • REBNY RLS Participant status
  • Proof of procuring cause (showing records, emails, etc.)

Compensation fields removed from RLS (Aug 1, 2025). Co-broke is now communicated off-RLS or via separate agreement. Verify co-broke amount BEFORE showing.

Example: Resale Co-Broke Calculation

Sale Price

$2,000,000

Co-Broke Offered

3%

Gross Commission

$60,000

Your Split (60%)

$36,000

UCBA Rules That Affect Your Commission (Resale)

BLOCKER

Buyer Rep Agreement Required BEFORE Any Showing (UCBA E7)

You must have a signed, written Buyer Representation Agreement with your client before taking them to ANY property. Without it, you have no legal basis for commission. This is both a REBNY rule and a NAR settlement requirement.

BLOCKER

No Compensation Data on RLS (UCBA G1)

The RLS does NOT collect or display any offers of compensation. All compensation fields were removed Aug 1, 2025. Co-broke must be confirmed directly with the listing brokerage before showing.

REQUIRED

Commission Negotiability Disclosure (UCBA G3)

You MUST disclose to clients that commissions are fully negotiable. This disclosure is required in the listing agreement, buyer representation agreement, and pre-closing documents.

RULE

Multiple Bids Disclosure (UCBA E17)

When there are competing offers on a property, the listing agent must disclose all offers to the seller. Competing bid amounts may be disclosed to co-brokers only if the seller authorizes it. All parties must be treated fairly.

RULE

Agreement Inspection (UCBA G4)

On request, you must provide listing agreements and/or buyer representation agreements to RLS staff for confidential inspection within 48 hours. Keep all agreements uploaded in the CRM Documents tab.

New Development (Sponsor) — RUNDBA Rules

When you bring a buyer to a new development project (Exhibit D of UCBA)

How Sponsor Commission Works

  1. Register your prospect IN WRITING at the Sales Office BEFORE introducing them to the property
  2. Arrange a confirmed appointment with the Exclusive Sales Agent during Sales Office hours
  3. Accompany your prospect on their first visit — this is critical
  4. Make sure the prospect names you as their broker on the Sign-In Sheet
  5. The Exclusive Sales Agent conducts the unit presentation (not you)
  6. Prospect submits a Purchase Agreement; Owner decides whether to accept
  7. If the deal closes, you earn your commission at closing

Net Purchase Price (What Commission is Based On)

INCLUDED in Net Purchase Price:

  • Purchase price from the Purchase Agreement
  • Storage unit purchase price
  • Parking space purchase price
  • Other facilities purchased/licensed

DEDUCTED from Net Purchase Price:

  • Credits on closing statement
  • Concessions or buyer incentives
  • Price reductions given to close

NOT deducted / NOT added:

  • Special upgrades ordered by buyer (not added)
  • Post-contract condition credits (not deducted)

14 Ways to LOSE Your New Development Commission

1. Offering Plan is abandoned or withdrawn
2. You were not the sole procuring cause of the sale
3. Prospect was already registered with Owner or Exclusive Sales Agent
4. Prospect is your family member or employee (unless Owner approves)
5. You failed to register the prospect IN WRITING before introducing them
6. You are not on the Sign-In Sheet, or prospect says "no broker"
7. Prospect was already registered with a different broker
8. You did NOT accompany prospect on their first visit (with narrow exceptions)
9. Prospect never visited the Sales Office before making an offer
10. A related party (co-purchaser, guarantor, family) already registered with another broker
11. Prospect claims you abandoned them or gave ineffective representation
12. Purchase Agreement names a different broker
13. Prospect has a buyer broker agreement with someone else
14. Prospect made 2+ unrepresented visits to the sales office before submitting an offer

Co-Brokers in New Development

  • Only ONE total commission paid per unit, even if you use a co-broker
  • Owner can pay jointly to you and your co-broker
  • Owner has no obligation regarding any co-broke agreement between you and your co-broker
  • Only Non-RLS Participant brokers need to physically sign the RUNDBA

Advertising Restriction (New Dev)

You CANNOT advertise new development units independently — no print, no online, no social media. Only use materials provided by the Exclusive Sales Agent, and only as they permit. Violation = material breach of the entire agreement.

Rental Commission

Who pays, how much, and how to get paid on rental deals

OP

Owner Pays

Landlord pays the full broker fee.

Typical: 1 month rent or 12-15% of annual rent

Split: If you're tenant's agent, co-broke is typically 50% of total fee

TP

Tenant Pays

Tenant pays the broker fee directly.

Typical: 1 month rent or 12-15% of annual rent

Note: Must be disclosed to tenant upfront

SPLIT

Owner + Tenant Split

Fee is split between landlord and tenant.

Typical: 50/50 or negotiated

Note: Both parties must agree in writing

Example: Rental Commission

Monthly Rent

$4,000

Annual Rent

$48,000

Fee (15%)

$7,200

Your Split (60%)

$4,320

FARE Act (NYC): Not yet live. When enacted, it may restrict who pays the broker fee on rentals. Until then, current OP/TP/Split rules apply. Use MoveInCosts field + PublicRemarks to disclose fees. Track updates via REBNY bulletins.

REQUIRED

Tenant Multiple-Fee Disclosure (UCBA E20)

If a tenant has agreed to pay the broker fee (TP) and is being shown apartments by multiple brokerages, you MUST inform the tenant they could owe fees to multiple firms. Disclose this risk upfront and in writing before showing.

Required Agreements Checklist

What you need signed BEFORE you can earn commission

Buyer Broker Agreement

Required BEFORE showing any property to a buyer

Must be in writing and signed by buyer
Must specify commission amount or rate
Must have a defined term (start + end date)
Keep a copy in your files and upload to CRM

RUNDBA — New Development Agreement

Required when bringing buyers to new development projects

RLS Participants are automatically bound (no signature needed)
Non-RLS brokers must sign before showing
Commission rate specified per project
Auto-terminates after 3 years

Exclusive Listing Agreement

Required when YOU are the listing agent (seller's side)

Signed by seller/landlord
Specifies commission rate and co-broke offered
Includes listing term and marketing permissions
Required before listing on RLS

Rental Commission Agreement

Confirms who pays the fee and how much on a rental

Specify OP, TP, or Split
Written before lease signing
Include fee amount and payment timeline
Disclose fee structure to all parties

Protect Your Commission

Steps to ensure you get paid on every deal

Documentation

  • Get ALL agreements signed BEFORE showing
  • Keep copies of every signed document
  • Upload agreements to CRM Documents tab
  • Save all email trails with clients and other brokers
  • Log all showing dates and times in CRM

Registration (New Dev)

  • Register prospects IN WRITING before introducing them
  • Include: your name, salesperson name, prospect's name/address/phone, date
  • ALWAYS accompany prospect on first visit
  • Ensure prospect writes YOUR name on the Sign-In Sheet
  • Get a copy of the Sign-In Sheet for your records

Timeline

  • Verify co-broke amount BEFORE showing (especially resale — comp fields removed from RLS)
  • Confirm RUNDBA commission rate before bringing buyer to new dev
  • Submit commission invoice/bill to Owner BEFORE closing (new dev)
  • Follow up on payment within 48 hours of closing
  • Submit commission request in CRM immediately after closing

Avoid These Mistakes

  • Showing a property without a signed buyer broker agreement
  • Letting a prospect visit a new dev Sales Office alone
  • Forgetting to register your prospect in writing (new dev)
  • Advertising new development units independently (material breach)
  • Assuming the co-broke amount without verifying it

Confirmation Letter (New Dev — Before Closing)

The Owner may require you to deliver a letter at or before closing confirming that you are the sole broker who procured the buyer. Prepare this in advance. Without it, the Owner can withhold your commission.

Commission Disputes

What happens when there's a disagreement about who gets paid

Resale (UCBA) Disputes

  • Governed by UCBA arbitration rules
  • REBNY arbitration panel resolves commission disputes
  • Contact broker (Maya) immediately if a dispute arises

New Development (RUNDBA) Disputes

  • Commission disputes go to REBNY binding arbitration
  • Disputed commission held in REBNY escrow until resolved
  • Other disputes: NY Supreme Court (NY County) or SDNY Federal Court
  • Prevailing party entitled to attorney fees
  • You may be required to provide an affidavit to support your claim

What to Do If You Have a Commission Dispute

  1. Notify Maya (broker) immediately — do not contact the other party directly
  2. Gather all documentation: agreements, emails, showing records, sign-in sheets
  3. Write a timeline of events (dates, who was present, what was said)
  4. The brokerage will handle the formal dispute process on your behalf
  5. Do NOT make statements to the other brokerage without broker approval

If a New Dev Agreement is Terminated

  • Owner can terminate with 15 days written notice (no cause needed)
  • Immediate termination for material breach by you
  • You still get paid for prospects registered BEFORE termination (if all other conditions are met)
  • Exception: if terminated for your material breach — no commission on transactions involving the breach

REBNY Penalties & Fines

UCBA 2026 violation escalation schedule — fines come out of YOUR commission

Fair Housing Violations (Zero Tolerance)

Offense Fine Cure Period
1st violation$2502 business days
2nd violation$500 + RLS TERMINATIONImmediate

A second Fair Housing violation permanently terminates your RLS access. No discriminatory language in listings, ads, or remarks — ever. Includes race, color, religion, sex, national origin, disability, familial status, age, sexual orientation, gender identity, lawful source of income, and all NYC Human Rights Law protected classes.

Data Quality Violations (Escalating)

Offense Fine Cure Period
1st violation$0 (warning)3 business days
2nd violation$2502 business days
3rd violation$2501 business day
4th violationRLS TERMINATIONNone

Examples: incomplete mandatory fields, incorrect data, wrong status, missing required photos. Cure periods shrink each time. 4th violation = permanently lose RLS access.

Incurable Violations (No Cure Period)

Offense Fine
1st incurable violation in calendar year$250
Each subsequent incurable violation$500

Examples: advertising an Owner Opt-Out property, displaying Participant Only listings publicly, using "Off-Market" language.

General UCBA Violations (Escalating Within 12 Months)

Offense Penalty
1st violation$500
2nd within 12 monthsUp to $2,000
3rd within 12 monthsUp to $10,000 + posted on REBNY website
4th within 12 monthsSuspension up to 30 days + posted on REBNY

Quarterly Brokerage-Level Fines

>5% Rejection Rate (Per Quarter)

$10,000

Must pay within 3 days

3 Quarterly Fines in 1 Year

30-Day Suspension

Must demonstrate corrective measures

This is why data quality matters. One agent's sloppy listings can trigger a $10K quarterly fine for the entire brokerage. All fines must be paid within 10 days or RLS access is terminated.

Important Notes

  • All fines must be paid within 10 days — failure = termination of RLS access
  • Unpaid fines after 60 days: broker is notified, 30 days to pay or suspension
  • Violations are waived if notice is served >180 days after listing is sold/canceled/expired
  • Complaints must be filed within 90 days of discovery
  • Good-faith resolution must be attempted before filing a formal complaint

Sources: REBNY Universal Co-Brokerage Agreement (UCBA), January 2026 revision | REBNY Universal New Development Brokerage Agreement (RUNDBA), Exhibit D, copyright 2025 | NAR Settlement Practice Changes (August 2024)

    Listing Type & Classification

    Owner Opt-Out Selected

    Per REBNY UCBA Art. I, Sec. 5(A): NO public dissemination whatsoever. All distribution channels will be disabled including IDX, Syndication, Listhub, NY MLS, Realtor, RPX, and WWW.

    Allowed: One-to-one personal phone calls and individual emails to RLS Participants only.

    Owner Opt-Out form (Exhibit B) must be signed and submitted via LMP within 48 hours.

    Violation = Incurable: $250 first offense, $500 each subsequent.

    Ours Alone — Non-RLS Listing

    Definition: An oral/verbal listing with no written exclusive agreement. The RLS does not accept Ours Alone listings (UCBA Art. I, Sec. 4).

    Distribution: This listing can ONLY appear on mallan.nyc (WWW) and StreetEasy (manual upload). All RLS, IDX, and syndication channels are disabled.

    Rules:

    • No RLS submission — listing is NOT on the REBNY Listing Service
    • No IDX distribution — other broker websites will NOT display this listing
    • No syndication to Realtor.com, Listhub, NY MLS, or any portal
    • No commission protection — no written exclusive agreement means limited legal protection
    • Seller can give the listing to other brokers simultaneously
    • UCBA rules do NOT apply (only governs Exclusive Listings on RLS)
    • Fair Housing Act + NY DOS advertising laws STILL apply to all marketing

    Recommended: Convert to Exclusive with a signed listing agreement for full RLS distribution and commission protection.

      Buyer Deal Process

      Buyer Portal

      Step-by-step guide from search to closing

      Cash Purchase (Hides mortgage-related steps)
      1

      Get a Real Estate Attorney

      Required for all NYC real estate transactions

      Required

      Recommendation: Hire a real estate attorney before making an offer. In NYC, attorneys review the contract, negotiate terms, conduct due diligence, and oversee the closing. This is standard practice and highly recommended even though not legally required.

      2

      Get Mortgage Pre-Approval

      Required if financing the purchase

      Financing

      Drag & drop pre-approval letter here or

      3

      Arrange Title Company

      Title search and insurance for condo purchases

      Condo

      Required for condo purchases. Co-ops use the corporation's attorney for title-related matters since shares are personal property, not real property.

      4

      Schedule Home Inspection

      Evaluate the property's condition before committing

      Optional
      5

      Prepare Your Offer

      Structure and submit your purchase offer

      Required
      6

      Contract Negotiation

      Attorney review, counter-offers, and contract execution

      Required
      Offer
      Submitted
      Counter
      Offer
      Offer
      Accepted
      Contract
      Signed
      Status: Awaiting Counter-Offer
      7

      Deposit Funds

      Contract deposit held in escrow (typically 10%)

      Required

      Wire Fraud Warning

      ALWAYS verify wire transfer instructions by calling your attorney directly using a known phone number. Never rely on emailed wire instructions alone. Hackers frequently intercept real estate transactions to redirect funds.

      8

      Board Application

      Required for co-op and condo purchases

      Co-op / Condo
      Application Progress 0 / 9 Documents

      9

      Board Interview Preparation

      Required for co-op purchases only

      Co-op Only
      Dress professionally — Business casual at minimum; err on the side of formal
      Be punctual — Arrive 5-10 minutes early; never late
      Know your finances — Be prepared to discuss income, assets, and debt comfortably
      Be friendly and personable — The board wants to know you'll be a good neighbor
      Don't discuss renovations — Even if you plan them, save it for after approval
      Bring your partner — If purchasing together, both should attend

      Verify the property condition before closing

      Income Qualification Calculator

      Check if income meets NYC rental requirements

      $
      $
      No

      Standard Requirement (No Guarantor)

      With Guarantor

      Qualification Status:
      Enter rent and income to check
      1

      Proof of Income

      Pay stubs (2-3 most recent), employment letter, or tax returns

      Landlords typically require proof of income equal to 40x the monthly rent. Accepted documents include recent pay stubs, an employment verification letter on company letterhead, or federal tax returns.

      Pay Stubs

      PDF, JPG, PNG

      Employment Letter

      PDF, JPG, PNG

      Tax Returns

      PDF, JPG, PNG

      2

      Guarantor Documentation (if needed)

      Same income documentation from your guarantor

      A guarantor must earn at least 80x the monthly rent. The guarantor typically must reside in the tri-state area (NY, NJ, CT) unless a third-party guarantor service is used.

      $

      Upload Guarantor Income Documentation

      PDF, JPG, PNG (pay stubs, tax returns, bank letter)

      3

      Employment Verification Letter

      Official letter on company letterhead confirming employment details

      Letter Must Include:

      • Employee full legal name
      • Job title / position
      • Employment start date
      • Annual salary or hourly rate
      • Company letterhead with contact information
      • Signature of HR representative or supervisor
      Download Template Word / PDF format

      Upload Employment Verification Letter

      PDF, JPG, PNG

      4

      Bank Letter / Proof of Funds

      Official bank verification of account and balance

      Must be on bank letterhead, dated within 30 days.

      $

      Upload Bank Letter

      PDF, JPG, PNG

      5

      Tax Returns with W-2

      Most recent 2 years of federal tax returns

      If you filed an extension or amended return, include proof of the extension along with the prior year's return. Self-employed applicants should include Schedule C or K-1 forms.

      Tax Year 2025

      Upload 2025 Return + W-2

      PDF, JPG, PNG

      Tax Year 2024

      Upload 2024 Return + W-2

      PDF, JPG, PNG

      6

      Recent Pay Stubs

      2-3 most recent pay periods

      Must show employer name, gross pay, and YTD earnings. Digital pay stubs from ADP, Gusto, or similar payroll systems are accepted.

      Upload Pay Stubs (2-3 most recent)

      PDF, JPG, PNG — multiple files accepted

      7

      Bank Statements

      2-3 most recent months of bank statements

      All pages required, including blank pages. Do not skip any pages or the application may be rejected. Statements must be consecutive months.

      Upload Bank Statements (2-3 months)

      PDF, JPG, PNG — multiple files accepted

      8

      Guarantor Documents (if applicable)

      Employment letter, tax returns, pay stubs, bank statements from guarantor

      Your guarantor must provide the same documentation as the tenant: employment verification letter, tax returns with W-2 (2 years), recent pay stubs, and bank statements.

      Employment Verification Letter

      Upload Guarantor Employment Letter

      Tax Returns with W-2 (2 years)

      Upload Guarantor Tax Returns + W-2

      Upload Guarantor Pay Stubs

      Bank Statements (2-3 months)

      Upload Guarantor Bank Statements

      9

      Board Application (if condo/co-op)

      Board package and management company requirements

      Board approval may take 2-6 weeks for co-ops. Condo boards typically have a right of first refusal (30-day review). Have all documents ready before submitting the application.

      Pocket Listings Are Prohibited

      Under the REBNY Universal Co-Brokerage Agreement (UCBA) Art. I Sec. 5(D) and the Clear Cooperation Policy:

      • All exclusive listings must be entered into the REBNY RLS within 24 hours
      • Maintaining listings outside the RLS ("pocket listings") is a violation
      • Penalties: $500 first offense → $2,000 → $10,000 → suspension

      Use Coming Soon status (sales only, max 14 days) for pre-marketing while remaining RLS-compliant.

      REBNY Rules Reference

      Quick reference for REBNY RLS co-brokerage and listing rules

      Co-Brokerage Commission Splits

      • Standard co-broke split: listing agent offers cooperating broker commission via RLS
      • Exclusive Right to Sell/Rent agreements must specify co-broke terms
      • Changes to co-broke commission require RLS update within 1 business day

      Listing Input Deadlines

      • Exclusive listings must be entered into RLS within 24 hours of signing
      • Price changes must be updated within 1 business day
      • Status changes (in-contract, closed) within 24 hours

      Showing & Open House Rules

      • Listing agent must respond to showing requests within a reasonable time
      • Open houses must be made available to all REBNY members
      • Broker open houses: listing agent sets date/time, all members welcome

      Common Violations

      • Advertising a listing without proper broker attribution
      • Failing to enter exclusive listings into RLS within 24 hours
      • Contacting another broker's exclusive client directly
      • Misrepresenting listing details or co-broke terms

      Marketing Hub

      E-Blasts, Social Media, Lead Magnets & Performance — RESO/REBNY Compliant

      Advertising Compliance — NY DOS & REBNY Rules MANDATORY

      NY DOS Advertising Rules (19 NYCRR §175.25)

      • Every ad MUST include brokerage name: Mallan Real Estate Inc.
      • Every ad MUST include office address OR phone
      • Agent or team name cannot appear without brokerage name
      • License #10991205323 on all brokerage materials

      REBNY / UCBA Prohibited in Marketing

      • No agent info (name, phone, URL) in listing descriptions or photos
      • No “Off-Market” language in any listing marketing
      • No compensation amounts or “free services” claims
      • Coming Soon: must show “No Showings until [date]”
      • IDX listings require attribution: “Courtesy of [Listing Broker]”
      • All content must comply with Fair Housing Act + NYC HRL
